name: Projection Deformation Topology Registry
purpose: Characterize how projections deform under translation, simplification, reduction, or sequentialization pressure.

deformation_modes.definition: Loss of concurrent aspect roles in favor of sequential or prioritized viewing.
Deformation that abstracts away memory or constraint history, making the projection appear memoryless.
Artificial reduction of projection tension, making discrete/smooth boundaries appear continuous.
Loss of analog granularity, forcing projection features into binary (0/1) states.
Loss of discrete boundaries, making distinct aspect roles appear as a single diffused field.
The most severe deformation, where projection distinctions are lost and the artifact is misread as a primitive.

risk_classes.definition: Projected form retains all critical features and loss-accounting accuracy.
Deformation affects the clarity of the source-relation link.
Deformation invites primitive promotion or physical identity claims.

governance_rules.rule: Every projection deformation must be categorized by mode and risk class.
Conflict smoothing deformations trigger automatic REJECT_ESCALATION.

forbidden_claims: Deformation smoothing derives physical vacuum states.
Binary freezing proves literal information theory as source.
Deformation risk metrics are optional for 'simple' projections.
